claimed_purpose.text: Exposes TeleMem's long-term memory operations as MCP tools so that any MCP-compatible client can store and retrieve memories through a local TeleMem instance.
TeleMem presents itself as a high-performance drop-in replacement for Mem0, re-exporting the mem0 API surface with its own classes layered on top.
TeleMem is characterized as having a comprehensive and advanced memory management system with multimodal extensions.
TeleMem is used as a long-term memory layer for chat engines.

mechanisms.text: The batch write path uses a buffer keyed by run_id and user_id scope. When the buffer reaches buffer_size, it is flushed. Flushing clusters all candidate and similar existing memories by cosine similarity before LLM fusion and write.
Write path — add: accepts either a single text statement or conversation turns (message log); optionally extracts salient facts via LLM before storing, or stores raw text as-is.
Each chunk of messages is summarized into a 20–100 character curated summary covering key nouns, times, and actions — this is the write path from raw log to curated memory
TeleMem buffers events up to a configurable maximum before flushing them to a vector store, distinguishing a transient event buffer from the persistent vector store.
The update step receives a set of similar (retrieved) memory fragments alongside the new memory fragment, implying retrieve-before-write for conflict/deduplication
Lore/events distinction: conversation-level event memories are stored under a dedicated pseudo-user 'events' and are always included in searches automatically.
search_mm() runs a ReAct-style agent (MMCoreAgent) with a THINK→ACTION→OBSERVATION loop to retrieve and reason over stored video memory using three tools
Per-user isolation: each user_id has an independent memory profile; a search scoped to one user_id never surfaces another character's private memories.
Write path (infer=False): each non-system message's content is stored verbatim with no LLM extraction call; message role is recorded in metadata.
Retrieve policy: search always includes shared 'events' memories regardless of user_id; results merged and ranked by score, optionally reranked.
The buffer key distinguishing event memories from person memories is derived from run_id plus user_id, with 'events' used when user_id is None.
Per-run message log: a deep copy of the base message list is taken at the start of each run, so conversation state is not shared across calls.
Video database is initialised from a caption path and embedding dimension and persisted on the instance for the lifetime of the agent.
Memory is written by calling add() with a message list and a user_id, persisting facts extracted from conversation turns.
Retrieve: search_memories performs semantic search and returns a single fused text passage, not ranked rows
Forget/delete surface inherited from mem0: delete, delete_all, reset available on the TeleMem object.
The integration pattern is retrieve-then-store: search() before answering, add() after each exchange.
Memory is written by calling add() after each turn and read by calling search() before responding.
Isolation: memory scope is per user_id, agent_id, or run_id; a default user scope is configurable
Uses faiss-cpu as a dependency, indicating vector-based retrieval is part of the memory mechanism
Change history: a memory_history tool exposes ADD/UPDATE/DELETE event log per memory_id.
TeleMem previously reported results on ZH-4O with deterministic multiple-choice scoring.
Memory is isolated per character, queryable by character identity
search() returns a mem0-compatible results shape.
Memory store is local (closed-world)

unknowns.text: The page describes memory_history as an MCP tool but does not document what it returns or whether it exposes a full operation log vs. a curated change history for a given memory entry.

Forget / explicit deletion from the FAISS+JSON store is available via MCP (delete_memory, delete_all_memories) but the README does not describe how deletion propagates to the FAISS index vs. the JSON metadata, or whether a hide-at-retrieve soft-delete option exists.

Conflict / supersession policy when add() produces a new fact that contradicts an existing stored memory is not described beyond 'LLM semantic clustering merges similar memories'; the page does not explain how contradictions are resolved vs. merged.

The flush mechanism from buffer to vector store (exact write/update/delete logic, conflict resolution beyond similarity thresholding) is not described in this config file; as a canonical config for a memory system it should specify these behaviors.

The page describes the MCP tool surface but does not document conflict or supersession behavior: what happens when add_memory is called with information that contradicts an existing stored memory (merge, overwrite, or append).
The retrieve policy for search_memories is not specified beyond semantic search: no detail on when the model is instructed to stay silent, threshold filtering, or adaptive retrieval behavior.
Forget behavior (delete from store vs hide at retrieve vs omit in generation) is not described for TeleMem's own layer; only inherited mem0 method names are listed without semantics.
Retrieve policy for when to stay silent (adaptive retrieval, relevance gating before injection into prompt) is not described; page only covers the search() API parameters.
Forget / delete behavior: this is a top-level architecture page but does not describe any delete-from-store or hide-at-retrieve mechanism.
Retrieve policy: the page shows vector search + rerank is always invoked on query but does not describe adaptive retrieval, silence conditions, or how many results are injected into the prompt.
Log vs memory distinction: no description of whether full conversation transcripts are stored separately from curated facts/summaries.
No description of forget/delete path for stored video memory (frames, captions, or vector DB entries)
No description of isolation model: whether video memory is scoped per user, session, agent, or shared
No description of conflict or supersession behavior when the same video is re-added or captions change

The page is an issue asking whether a technical report exists and when it will be released, implying no architectural or API documentation is yet publicly available. Core memory behaviors (persist, retrieve, forget, conflict/supersession) are entirely undescribed.

The evaluation charter page (https://teleai-uagi.github.io/telemem/evaluation/) is referenced as the canonical source for evaluation and reporting rules but its contents are not reproduced here; persist, retrieve, forget, and conflict behaviors may be specified there.
No information on forget/delete behavior, conflict resolution, or isolation (per-user, per-session, per-agent) is present on this page despite it referencing the core add/search API.
Forget / delete path: this canonical issue for the memory API mentions add and search but says nothing about deleting or superseding stored facts.

Retrieve policy: the page does not specify whether memories are always injected into every turn or retrieved adaptively (e.g., only when relevant above a threshold). The search() API offers a threshold parameter but the scaffold's retrieval policy for automatic injection is not described.
Forget/deletion behavior from the memory store is not described
Retrieve policy (always retrieve vs adaptive) is not described
